pr.title: fix(comm): Lamport clear size in 16-bit units shared by every writer; fence the Helix sender before refilling shared memory
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Two fixes to the TRT-LLM-derived communication kernels, from upstream TensorRT-LLM commits FlashInfer's copies predate.

- **Lamport clear size kept in elements of the writer's dtype** ([NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#21283](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/21283)). `LamportComm` in `trtllm_allreduce_fusion.cuh` and `trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion.cuh` recorded `params.size * NRanks` elements for the next kernel to clear, and that kernel divided by its own `VEC_SIZE`. Every Lamport kernel on a workspace shares the slot. The Python wrapper refuses a call whose dtype disagrees with the workspace's `use_fp32_lamport`, so the mismatch needs a lower-level call that bypasses that check on a workspace created with `use_fp32_lamport=True`: a bf16 kernel following an fp32 one then cleared half the bytes and read stale data, and the reverse over-cleared. Within one dtype the old count was right; the fix makes the slot's unit independent of the writer. The slot now counts 16-bit units and readers round up to whole 16-byte stores. Upstream switched the slot to bytes; FlashInfer cannot, because the cake kernels on the same workspace (`csrc/cake_trtllm_moe_allreduce_union/`, `csrc/cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion/`, 36 generated files) write bf16 / fp16 element counts and read `clear_size / 8`. Two-byte units keep bf16 / fp16 bitwise as before, stay compatible with cake, and still fix fp32. The workspace layout is unchanged (`kernel_flag_ptr[4]`, initialized to 0); its docstring now names the unit (`5da38d8bc`).
- **Lamport clear stores wrote the clearing kernel's own `-0`** (FlashInfer-side, found in review). A bf16 / fp16 kernel cleared with `0x8000` pairs, which an fp32 kernel two calls later reads as `0x80008000`, not fp32 `-0`, and takes as arrived data. The clear now writes the fp32 `-0` pattern (`0x80000000` per word) whatever the dtype: fp32 readers see `-0`, bf16 / fp16 readers (trtllm and cake both test each 16-bit half) see `0x8000` in the high half. Remaining gap, not touched here: the cake kernels still clear with bf16 `-0` pairs, so cake followed by an fp32 trtllm kernel on one workspace is still unsafe; no caller does that today.
- **Helix all-to-all sender refill ordering** ([NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#20939](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20939), fence part). In `helixAllToAll.cu` the sender's `protoPack` stores and the register S2G loads go through the generic proxy, and the next iteration refills the same shared memory with `cp.async.bulk` (async proxy) without a fence between them. A `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` before the `__syncwarp` orders them, matching the receiver side that #5172 already fenced.

## 🔍 Related Issues

[NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#21283](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/21283), [NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#20939](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/20939).

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

The existing multi-rank tests (`tests/comm/test_trtllm_allreduce_fusion*.py`, `test_trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion*.py`, `test_dcp_alltoall.py`) cover the touched kernels; they need 2+ GPUs, which the development node does not have, so this PR relies on the GitLab multi-GPU lane. Local: the `trtllm_comm` and DCP all-to-all JIT modules build on the branch (CUDA 13.0 CI container). `trtllm_comm`, `dcp_alltoall` and `dcp_alltoall_generated` built on B200 in the CUDA 13.0 CI container.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.


## Reviewer Notes

Upstream also moved the clear size to a 64-bit slot in a new workspace word; FlashInfer keeps the existing `int` slot because `clear_size <= lamport_comm_size`, which the Python side caps at `MAX_COMM_SIZE`. The bf16-after-fp32 case needs a workspace used with both dtypes, and the cake interplay a workspace alternating `backend="trtllm"` / `"cake"` with different inputs; no existing test does either, and same-input A/B runs pass even when stale data is read. A mixed-dtype / mixed-backend case would be the regression test if reviewers want one. The GitLab lane for the latest push includes `test_cake_moe_allreduce_union.py` and `test_cake_moe_finalize_allreduce.py`.
